release.name: v1.5.0
release.body:
# WaterWall v1.50

WaterWall v1.50 introduces **live user administration, more resilient authentication, per-user bandwidth controls, and reliability improvements**.

Building on the previous release’s stream and packet forwarding improvements, this release also refines routing, multiplexing, TUN processing, TLS behavior, and resource management, while adding new transport options.

## Live administration API and command-line tools

The new `APIServer` and bundled Python administration client make it possible to manage supported nodes and accounts while WaterWall is running.

Operators can inspect status, browse accounts, create users, change passwords, update quotas and expiry settings, and enable or disable access. Explicit permissions control available operations, and conditional updates help prevent conflicting administrative edits.

AuthenticationServer also gains optional rotating audit logs for administrative changes, alongside improved database saving, backup handling, and recovery.

The administration client requires **Python 3.10 or later** and uses only the standard library.

[Administration client documentation](https://github.com/radkesvat/WaterWall/tree/main/tunnels/APIServer/client)

You can currently manage Vless,Trojan,Socks5,HttpProxy protocols with current AuthenticationClient.

## More resilient authentication and accounting

After a successful synchronization, AuthenticationClient can continue admitting previously synchronized users during temporary authentication-server outages. Cached quotas, expiry settings, and local connection and IP limits remain enforced, and accumulated usage is reported when connectivity returns.

Usage reporting now handles reconnects more reliably, preserving pending reports and preventing matching retries from charging the same traffic twice. Larger account databases synchronize in pages, and an interrupted refresh preserves the previous usable account cache.

The authentication cache and pending usage remain **in memory**, so this continuity applies while the processes remain running.

## Per-user bandwidth and quota controls

UserController now supports separate **upload and download bandwidth limits**, shared across a user’s connections within one AuthenticationClient.

A new `traffic-multiplier` setting controls how measured traffic counts toward quotas. For example, `0.5` counts half the transferred bytes, while `2` counts double. Its default is `1`, and bandwidth limits continue to use actual transferred bytes.

## Forwarding, routing, and resource improvements

- **Linux TUN multiqueue:** TunDevice now attempts to distribute receive queues across workers by default, with a single-queue fallback when multiqueue setup is unavailable.
- **Packet batching:** TUN and RawSocket output use worker-local batches, with additional TCP acknowledgement batching and more buffering headroom in the packet-to-connection stack.
- **RAM-aware splice allocation:** Linux splice pipes are allocated on demand within limits that consider the RAM profile, detected memory limits, and file descriptor headroom.
- **Incremental MUX delivery:** Available stream data can reach a child connection without waiting for the entire MUX frame to arrive. Paused-child buffering also receives fixes.
- **Less processing after setup:** Eligible protocol nodes bypass their completed setup handlers once a TCP connection is ready.
- **More accurate routing:** Fixes cover fragmented TLS ClientHello detection, HTTP/2 request selection, UDP datagram replay, route-target binding, interface-specific listener dispatch, and GeoSite keyword matching.
- **Reverse connections:** New activation handling supports destinations that send first, allowing a server greeting to reach a client that has not sent application data.
- **Fixed packet-bridge destinations:** ConnectionToPackets gains optional `target-address` and `port` settings for direct fixed-destination forwarding.

## Reliability and platform fixes

Unsupported IPv4 fragments reaching the packet/connection bridges are now dropped instead of terminating WaterWall. Fake DNS mappings retain their domain identity until the advertised TTL expires, avoiding premature address reuse.

Other fixes include:

- Correct source-IP tracking for authenticated Trojan, VLESS, and SOCKS5 UDP traffic.
- Zero-length UDP datagram handling in VLESS, when supported by the peer.
- Stricter configuration, CIDR, authentication-request, and account-import validation.
- Improved credential and API-token cleanup.
- Correct Windows TUN MTU configuration and clearer Wintun diagnostics.
- Improved oversized-packet handling on macOS and BSD.
- Correct BSD TUN address assignment and better Linux default-route discovery.
- Explicit bounds on additional TUN receive queues and packet handoff storage.

## TLS and HTTP improvements

- **TLS session resumption** lets TlsClient reuse eligible sessions through a bounded cache.
- Optional **Encrypted ClientHello**, configured through `ech-config-list`, protects the inner server name when the destination supports ECH. Configured ECH requires acceptance rather than falling back to exposing that name.
- Updated BoringSSL, TLS handshake settings, and HTTP framing bring these paths closer to the project’s Chrome reference.
- RealityServer receives corrections to camouflage fallback handling.

## New QUIC transport option

New `QuicClient` and `QuicServer` nodes carry application streams over **QUIC v1 with TLS 1.3 encryption**.

These nodes provide a transport for paired WaterWall deployments; they do not implement HTTP/3.

[QUIC configuration examples and certificate setup](https://github.com/radkesvat/WaterWall/tree/main/tunnels/QuicClient/examples)

## Before upgrading

- **Upgrade AuthenticationClient and AuthenticationServer together.** Their authentication, synchronization, and accounting messages have changed. Custom protocol clients also need updating.
- **Upgrade ReverseClient and ReverseServer together** because reverse connections now use an activation prefix.
- Give each independently running AuthenticationClient instance its own identity in the server’s `auth-clients` list.
- Manually configured UserController nodes now require `payload-mode`: `stream`, `datagram`, or `dest_context->protocol`. Automatically inserted controllers supply this internally.
- MUX’s default parent write pause/resume thresholds are now **128 MiB / 4 MiB**. The resume threshold no longer derives from a custom pause threshold. UDP over MUX requires explicit datagram framing, such as `UdpOverTcpClient` and `UdpOverTcpServer`.
- When enabling APIServer, every loaded configuration needs a unique, nonempty logical `name`. Use a verified encrypted transport for remote administration; API authentication alone does not encrypt traffic.

**Full changelog:** [v1.46.96 → v1.50](https://github.com/radkesvat/WaterWall/compare/v1.46.96...v1.50)
